news.title: CONCACAF Make Gianni Infantino Request Amid FIFA World Cup Fallout - He Ignores It
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino ignored a direct request from the president of CONCACAF not to attend a youth tournament being held in the Caribbean, instead making a public appearance at the event anyway, according to France 24. An under-14 football tournament, organised by the North American football confederation, CONCACAF, was held in the Dominican Republic on Saturday. Infantino was initially invited to the event, but after recent controversies surrounding FIFA's governance of the game, the president was asked not to show his face. However, Infantino posted photos on his Instagram account that documented his arrival in the Caribbean nation on Friday, before he then attended the tournament on Saturday.

news.title: Arsenal superstar Bukayo Saka shrugs off World Cup heartbreak and injury agony with secret seven-day fitness regime
news.lede: BUKAYO SAKA could be forgiven for starting this season slowly and with a World Cup hangover. The winger endured a frustrating tournament and his hat-trick in England’s third-place play-off win over France came in only a third start. But there were no lingering signs of that disappointment — nor the Achilles issue that had dogged Saka since March – on Friday night. He was electric and scored Arsenal’s second goal as the champions began their title defence with a convincing 3-0 win over Coventry.

news.title: ‘See you at the hairdresser’s’: Gianni Infantino’s bizarre reply to bald reporter
news.lede: Fifa president tells Sky man: ‘You have a nice haircut’. Defies Concacaf president plea to stay away ​from event. Gianni Infantino told a reporter “I’ll see you at the hairdresser’s” after he was asked whether he had betrayed football over his aborted World Cup sell-off plan. The Fifa president was stopped outside a hotel in the Dominican Republic by the Sky News US correspondent, James Matthews, who challenged the under-fire leader of football’s governing body over why he had not resigned, despite calls from across the game for him to step down.

news.title: Andy Burnham says he wants to bring men’s World Cup back to UK in 2042
news.lede: PM tells regional mayors during informal discussions he is keen for tournament to return to British Isles. Andy Burnham has said he wants to bring the men’s World Cup to the UK in 2042, returning the tournament to Britain for the first time in almost eight decades. During informal discussions at No 10 North in Manchester on Friday, the prime minister told regional mayors he was keen for the tournament to be played in the British Isles. The World Cup took place in England in 1966, when the home side beat West Germany 4-2 in the final after extra time – the only time the country has either hosted or won the contest.

news.title: UK considering bid to host 2042 FIFA World Cup
news.lede: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has proposed a bid to host the 2042 FIFA World Cup, according to The Times. As reported by İdman.Biz, citing the British newspaper, the idea was raised during a meeting with city mayors at the Prime Minister’s new office in Manchester. According to the report, Burnham is currently discussing the possibility of submitting a bid for the tournament with the Football Association (FA) and the Premier League. England has hosted the FIFA World Cup only once, in 1966.
